newsitem.title: JAPAN: Kawasaki Steel to raise price of China-bound steel.
newsitem.headline: Kawasaki Steel to raise price of China-bound steel.

text.p: Kawasaki Steel Corp said on Wednesday it had agreed with China to increase the price of its steel products bound for China by about five percent.
Kawasaki Steel said China National Metals & Minerals Import & Export Corp had accepted an increase in the price of its steel products to be shipped from August 1997 to January 1998.

Kawasaki said the five percent price rise will affect cold-rolled sheets, galvanised steel sheets and thick steel sheets, while the price for other steel products such as hot-rolled sheets and tin plates will post smaller increases.
The volume to be shipped during the August-January period is expected to be 20 to 30 percent bigger than the preceding February 1997 to July 1997 period, a Kawasaki spokesman said.
During February to July, Kawasaki will ship about 10,000 to 15,000 tonnes a month to China, he added.

Other four major steel makers -- Nippon Steel Corp, NKK Corp, Kobe Steel Ltd and Sumitomo Metal Industries -- said earlier this month they had separately agreed with China National Metals to raise their China-bound steel product prices by about five percent.
